claim: Art. 27(3): substantive decisions need P5 concurrence; the duty of a party to a dispute to abstain applies only under Chapter VI (not Chapter VII enforcement)
author: United Nations
credentials: The UN's founding treaty text, published by the UN
publication: Charter of the United Nations, Chapter V
title: Chapter V: The Security Council (Articles 23-32) | United Nations
quote: Decisions of the Security Council on all other matters shall be made by an affirmative vote of nine members including the concurring votes of the permanent members; provided that, in decisions under Chapter VI, and under paragraph 3 of Article 52, a party to a dispute shall abstain from voting.

claim: Feb 2022: Russia vetoed a resolution demanding it stop its own attack on Ukraine and withdraw, though 11 of 15 members voted in favour
author: UN News
credentials: Official news service of the United Nations
title: Russia blocks Security Council action on Ukraine | UN News
quote: Russia vetoed a UN Security Council resolution on Friday that would have demanded that Moscow immediately stop its attack on Ukraine and withdraw all troops ... While 11 of the Council’s 15 members voted in favour of the text, China India, and the United Arab Emirates abstained.

claim: July 2023: a 13-of-15 resolution renewing the Bab al-Hawa aid crossing (lifeline for four million in NW Syria) was struck down by one Russian no vote
author: UN News
credentials: Official news service of the United Nations
title: Security Council fails to reach consensus on Syria aid lifeline | UN News
quote: the Bab al-Hawa crossing point – a lifeline for four million people in northwest Syria, the last opposition stronghold. ... Although 13 of the 15 countries in the Council voted in favour of the resolution, it was struck down by a no vote from Russia, one of the five permanent members.

claim: Sept 2025: the US vetoed a Gaza ceasefire/aid resolution backed by the other 14 members amid famine - its sixth ceasefire veto of the war
author: UN News
credentials: Official news service of the United Nations
title: Security Council: US votes against resolution on Gaza ceasefire | UN News
quote: The United States once again vetoed a UN resolution demanding an immediate, unconditional and permanent ceasefire in the Gaza Strip ... against the backdrop of famine spreading in the besieged enclave ... 14 members of this Council have sent a clear message ... Since then, the US has vetoed five other resolutions calling for a ceasefire, most recently in June.

claim: April 2024: GA President says the Council is unable to act on Gaza, Mali, Syria, Ukraine and DPRK; 13 vetoes since the 2022 'veto initiative', which is non-binding
author: UN News
credentials: Official news service of the United Nations, reporting the General Assembly President's statement
title: General Assembly debates Security Council’s rising veto use | UN News
quote: Assembly President Dennis Francis emphasised that the Security Council remains unable to collectively address critical peace and security situations in the Gaza Strip, Mali, Syria and Ukraine as well as concerning the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK). ... Vetoes have been used 13 times since the General Assembly adopted a resolution designed to foster greater cooperation with the Security Council following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in early 2022. ... As with all Assembly resolutions, they carry moral and political weight, but are non-binding

claim: Arts. 24-25: the Council exists to ensure 'prompt and effective action' on behalf of all members, and its decisions bind every UN member
author: United Nations
credentials: The UN's founding treaty text, published by the UN
publication: Charter of the United Nations, Chapter V
title: Chapter V: The Security Council (Articles 23-32) | United Nations
quote: In order to ensure prompt and effective action by the United Nations, its Members confer on the Security Council primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security, and agree that in carrying out its duties under this responsibility the Security Council acts on their behalf. ... The Members of the United Nations agree to accept and carry out the decisions of the Security Council in accordance with the present Charter.

claim: March 2022: Russia was outvoted 141 to 5 in the General Assembly on a resolution demanding it end its offensive in Ukraine
author: UN News
credentials: Official news service of the United Nations
title: General Assembly resolution demands end to Russian offensive in Ukraine | UN News
quote: A total of 141 countries voted in favour of the resolution, which reaffirms Ukrainian sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity. ... Five countries - Belarus, the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (more commonly known as North Korea) Eritrea, Russia and Syria - voted against it, while 35 abstained.

claim: March 2011: the Libya use-of-force resolution passed 10-0-5 with the veto in place - China and Russia abstained rather than block it
author: UN News
credentials: Official news service of the United Nations
title: Security Council authorizes ‘all necessary measures’ to protect civilians in Libya | UN News
quote: Acting under Chapter VII of the UN Charter, which provides for the use of force if needed, the Council adopted a resolution by 10 votes to zero, with five abstentions, authorizing Member States “to take all necessary measures… to protect civilians ... The abstentions included China and Russia, which have the power of veto, as well as Brazil, Germany and India.

claim: Two permanent members (France since 2013, UK recently) commit not to veto in mass atrocities; 127 states back the initiative; France has not vetoed since 1989 - only 2 of 5 P5 have joined
author: French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs
credentials: Official foreign ministry of a permanent Security Council member
title: France’s proposals to strengthen the United Nations | France Diplomatie
quote: France made a commitment in 2013 not to use its veto in the event of mass atrocities. ... Today, 127 States support the French-Mexican initiative, 20 of which have joined this initiative since the beginning of 2026. The United Kingdom is one of the States that recently joined the initiative, thereby becoming the second permanent member of the Security Council, alongside France, to do so. ... France has not used its veto since 1989.

claim: July 2025: India's foreign ministry said India does not subscribe to any unilateral sanction measures, in response to new EU sanctions on Russia's energy trade
author: The Tribune (quoting India's Ministry of External Affairs)
credentials: India's oldest English-language daily, reporting the official MEA spokesperson statement
title: There should be no double standards: India on European Union sanctions            - The Tribune
quote: India does not subscribe to any unilateral sanction measures, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said in response to the European Union announcing fresh punitive measures on Russia, especially on its energy trade.
